subject: VPC telemetry transfer: SIEM proof-of-delivery & trace hook validation
messages:
From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@aventurix.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: log handoff & SIEM proof for VPC/private deploy

Hi Connor,

We're prepping our audit package for the on-prem deployment you completed last month and need a short, verifiable proof that our SIEM ingestion is receiving the right telemetry from the Redwood forwarder inside our VPC. Specifically we need: 

- A time-bounded sample of logs (syslog + JSON app logs) showing ingestion into our Splunk HEC endpoint with timestamps and host metadata.
- Evidence of TLS+mutual auth (cert thumbprints / TLS handoff notes) and the HEC token exchange you used for the test ingest.
- A short trace sample showing trace IDs propagated from our app through the forwarder to the tracehook sink (span ids, sample payload).
- Confirmation of retention/rotation policy for the forwarded logs (how long Redwood keeps a copy, if any).

Can you provide these artifacts or confirm a 2-hour test window next week where we can validate end-to-end? Our compliance team likes to see a tarred evidence bundle and a one-page acceptance checklist.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform Ops, Aventurix
sam.jenkins@aventurix.com
+1 415 555 0198

Subject: Re: Request: log handoff & SIEM proof for VPC/private deploy

Thanks Sam — looping in our security and SE leads to put together an evidence bundle and an execution plan.

Kimberly / Ben / Lauren: can you own the artifacts below and confirm availability for a 2-hour test window? I expect we'll produce:

- A tarball with sample logs (syslog + structured JSON) covering a 30-minute window with UTC timestamps.
- A small trace sample (x-trace-id/x-span-id) mapped to the logs so your team can correlate.
- TLS handshake notes and the HEC token exchange record (redacted tokens).
- A one-page acceptance checklist matching Aventurix compliance criteria.

Sam: if you can confirm which SIEM tenant (host + HEC token) we'll point at and preferred test windows (PST morning usually works), we'll schedule.

I'll take point on the delivery and follow-up with the DocuSign transfer form for the evidence bundle (for your audit intake).

Connor
Connor O'Brien

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Below is the proposed evidence checklist and the minimal acceptance criteria; attaching the artifacts we'll produce.

Planned artifacts (attachments):
- avtr_evidence_snapshot_v1.tar.gz (contains siem-ingest-sample.log, mapping.csv, forwarder-metadata.json)
- tracehook-config.yaml (sample trace hook config we ran during the test)

Acceptance checklist (we will provide one-page CSV + one-line signoff per item):
1) Ingest proof: SPLUNK HEC events with timestamps between 2027-11-03T16:00:00Z and 2027-11-03T16:30:00Z that include host, pod/container id, and X-Trace-ID. (PASS if >95% of generated events appear)
2) TLS+auth proof: TLS server cert chain and client cert thumbprint used by forwarder; capture of TLS handshake success.
3) Token exchange: HEC token used in test (redacted) and a timestamped request log showing token header.
4) Trace continuity: at least one end-to-end trace where spans are present in both our trace collector and included in the ingested payload to Splunk.
5) Retention statement: documentation showing Redwood's temporary evidence retention policy for the bundle (we keep the snapshot for 30 days by default; full retention policy attached).

Proposed test window: 2027-11-03 09:00-11:00 PST (2027-11-03T17:00-19:00 UTC). We ask for a 15-min kickoff before the window to confirm endpoints.

If that works, Ben will run the tracehook validation and Lauren will coordinate the artifact handoff + DocuSign evidence transfer.

Kimberly Park
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: avtr_evidence_snapshot_v1.tar.gz, tracehook-config.yaml
